feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 5.0 N/mm, height flush-2 mm, comp 9 out, reb 10 out. Shock 56 N/mm, sag 105 mm, LSC 12 out, HSC 1.5 turns out, reb 10-11 out.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 5.0 N/mm, 2 mm height, comp 12 out, reb 9 out. Shock 56 N/mm, sag 105 mm, LSC 11 out, HSC 1.25-1.5 out, reb 10 out. Baseline aimed at comfort; solid front engine mounts help front traction.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 2 mm height, comp 8 out, reb 10. Shock sag 105, LSC 11 out, HSC 1.5 out, reb 12. 2025 shock spring 56 N/mm (2024: 58). New linkage gave 'better holdup' under acceleration, less pitching; one-piece 8 mm front mounts gave 'more front end bite'. Swapping 2025 linkage onto a 2024 needs lighter spring + revalve. Bike 'a little calmer' than 2024.

feedback.brand: Luxon; Twin Air; GYTR; Works Connection; Guts
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Forks slid down in clamps as far as possible to slacken head angle and reduce headshake; Luxon 23 mm offset calmed steering; tightened steering stem nut moderately as 'poor man's steering damper'; 49->48T rear made 2nd taller to cover 2nd+3rd and softened bark; went mellower than Yamaha's mellow map (2 map attempts); Twin Air PowerFlow gave 'slightly faster rev and more pull through the middle' (no backfire screen); GYTR hydraulic clutch preferred for 'broader modulation'; Pro Launch 130 mm (160 mm on grates); radiator cap 1.1 -> 1.8 kg/cm2 recommended; FMF and Pro Circuit preferred among exhausts.
feedback.measured: 59.48 hp (Husqvarna FC450 60.1 hp). 2025 fork pressure springs 20 N/mm vs 22 in 2024; shock 56 vs 58 N/mm.

feedback.brand: Luxon; Twin Air; Guts; Works Connection
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Forks dropped fully in clamps; Luxon 23 mm offset 'calmed down the steering and kept the front end tracking straight'; tested four progressively mellower maps and kept the mellowest; 49->48T rear; Twin Air PowerFlow faster rev/smoother power; FMF or Pro Circuit exhaust; holeshot 130/160 mm; WC peg brackets need 2022 or aftermarket pegs on 2024. Dislikes: dirt falls into throttle body at filter change, kill button above map button causes accidental map changes, stock Belleville clutch spring too soft, tall seat.

feedback.author: Jody Weisel
feedback.conditions: Reader complaint: snappy off-idle throttle causing wheelies landing jumps/exiting ruts on 2023-2024 YZ450F
feedback.observed: Yamaha optional 'Smooth Linear' map still had bark off idle. A Yamaha R&D map with more fuel between 2000-5000 rpm reduced crispness and bark; MXA still runs it on 2023-2024. 49->48T rear made 2nd taller, reduced thrust out of corners - helped but did not fully fix throttle response.
feedback.measured: Fuel/ignition table values only in an image on the page - not captured.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: 2026: new frame downtube, front mounts 4 mm R / 6 mm L (was 8 mm both), new shock (28 mm base valve, tool-less LSC), Nissin hydraulic clutch, intake cam 110->107 deg, +8% flywheel inertia, mid-pipe resonator + choked muffler, stock gearing 13/51. Lowered sag to 106-107 mm to take weight off the fork; fork 2 clicks stiffer compression held it higher. 13/51 stock preferred by fast riders; 50T preferred by vets; 49T 'not feasible for motocross'. Testers preferred 2026 airbox with stock 2025 exhaust; GYTR sells the 2025 airbox; XPR billet water outlet for <=2025 (Evans coolant melted plastic outlet); Twisted Development breather bypass; radiator cap to 1.8 kg/cm2.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Pre-test: triple clamps, fork/shock, wheels and muffler from 2025 fit 2026; older engine mounts fit but 2026 front mounts are different thickness for new frame; subframe does not carry over. Keefer ran heavier springs on 2023-2025 for comfort.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Stock 13/51 -> 13/50: 2026 feels short in 2nd and can't pull 3rd in corners; dropping a tooth makes 2nd more usable.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock 13/49 suits West Coast hard pack
feedback.observed: 13/50 for East Coast/deep dirt: better 2nd-gear recovery, into 3rd sooner, better 3rd-gear corner speed. 14/52: smoother roll-on, better shock feel under acceleration (less chain bind). Disagrees in direction with MXA, which went taller (48T) on 2024/2025 to tame the hit.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Mix of tacky rutted and shallow-rut square-edge tracks; sag 104-105 mm
feedback.observed: 23 mm ROCS: small lean gain, slightly less off-throttle twitch. 23.5 mm Ride Engineering (fork 3-3.5 mm): more front traction on lean, less headshake - his pick. 24 mm ROCS (fork 4 mm, needs Technical Touch offset stem): more planted on decel, firmer. 25 mm: lazy/vague in corners, best on GP/sand. Stock 22 mm fine for 2022, 2023 chassis benefits from more offset.

feedback.product: Fork + shock revalve, smaller bladder cap
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork: more holdup on decel bumps and comfort leaning under throttle. Shock: smaller bladder cap firmed initial load for more traction out of corners; more comfort on big bumpy downhills. Sag 105 mm.
feedback.measured: Prices: fork revalve $200, shock revalve $200, bladder cap $80, Enzo comp adjuster $250, oil/nitrogen $55.

feedback.author: Swapmoto staff (testers Foster, Maeda, Mascho, Puerner, Ray)
feedback.observed: Unanimous 450 winner. Testers raised fork 5 mm in clamps; sag set to 103 mm (Yamaha suggests 106 mm); Alex Ray ran 100 mm to put more weight on the front. Best fork in class; new linkage helps comfort. Dislikes: tiny crossbar pad, stubby front fender.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: No 2026 changes. Fork 4.7 N/mm, 3 mm, comp 8 out, reb 5-6 out. Shock 54 N/mm (from 56 with 2025 linkage), sag 105, HSC 1.25 out, LSC 9 out, reb 8 out. Slower rebound both ends calmed chassis; fork still rises too quickly on throttle mid-corner -> front washes out; riders <160 lb soften HSC to let rear squat on exits and help fork settle on braking bumps.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Same numbers as 2026 baseline (fork 4.7, 3 mm, C8, R5-6; shock 54, 105 mm, HSC 1.25, LSC 9, R8).

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 4.7 N/mm, 3 mm, C8, R5-6. Shock 56 N/mm, sag 105, HSC 1.5 out, LSC 12-14 out, R9. 2024 valving 'a little beefier', same springs; harder to dial in.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Riders wanted more fork support: 4 clicks stiffer fork compression and 1-2 slower rebound reduced off-throttle dive. Day-one settings: fork C7 R5, height 3-4 mm (stock 7 mm); shock LSC 11, HSC 1.25, R11; sag 104-105. Less low-end, more mid-top than 2023; 2nd gear 'super short' -> try 49T. Turns in lighter, less stable at tire edge, nervous chopping throttle. Seat unfriendly; muffler 'atrocious' noise. Yamaha tester's 'Stevie Map' with TC off smooths low-rpm richness.

feedback.product: KK Passive Aggressive / Keefer Free Feeling 2.0
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Millville (soft sand); deep early, broken-in afternoon
feedback.observed: Bike 'runs a little dirty/rich down low' stock. Passive Aggressive: more low-end pull and mid for 2nd-to-3rd; used early on deep track. Free Feeling 2.0: less engine braking, maybe less torque, stronger mid-top; used in afternoon. Gearing 13/49, changed to 13/50 at Millville for soft-sand traction. Must change TH% under 'POSITION' tab when loading.
feedback.measured: Map values not published in text.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Stock 13/50 -> 13/49: 2024-25 engine lost pulling power in 2nd; one tooth less lets 2nd pull longer and reduces shifting. Same recommendation repeated for 2026 (May 2026 guide). Note Keefer himself went 13/50 at Millville sand on 2024.

feedback.brand: Twin Air; Guts; Works Connection; GYTR
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: 50->49T rear lengthened each gear, easier to manage; 2nd short so shift early. Most testers lessen engine braking and increase throttle response in Power Tuner. For headshake drop forks in clamps or tighten stem nut. Suggested: Twin Air PowerFlow, Guts flat seat foam, WC fork clickers, 49T, hydraulic clutch. Dislikes: seat, filter lets dirt in, weaker bottom response than 2023, far-out clutch engagement, noise.

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.observed: Sag 105 mm worked for 150-200 lb testers. Most riders preferred the most aggressive of three Power Tuner maps ('into the meat of the power sooner and rev out longer'). Less impressive on low-speed choppy tracks; mid/top trails rivals; loud intake.

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Stiffer valving: forks compressed much less under braking, 'the shock wallow was gone', balanced front/rear. Vet testers preferred stock.

feedback.brand: XPR; FMF; Guts; Twin Air; Works Connection; FCP
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: XPR dual injector + Vortex: more bottom pull and rpm response, beat GYTR head/piston kit for initial response. FMF 4.1: more mid and a little top. Twin Air PowerFlow: better throttle response/bottom. Guts Wide Top foam ($99.99) lasts longer. WC Elite throttle tube ($74.95) smooth. FCP Race Cups 'done wonders' on 2025-2026 YZ450F (not tried on 250F).

feedback.author: Tokarski710 (Steve Tokarski, worked on bike development)
feedback.observed: Fork compression 'a couple of clicks stiffer', rebound 2 clicks open; fork height 2 mm -> flush best. Stronger top, +700 rpm over-rev; low-end maybe slightly down (sound rules). Shock excellent; fork has mid-stroke stopping point, harsh on small bumps. Hydraulic clutch on-off engagement helps rpm recovery. Suggested: aftermarket exhaust 'to unlock additional power', GYTR kit with airbox + FMF, MX34 tires.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 4.7 N/mm, 4 mm, C7, R11. Shock 56 N/mm, sag 104, HSC 7/8-1 out, LSC 9, R9. Same as 2022. Smoother linear map best for chassis/suspension feel. Some off-throttle pitching.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Fork 4.2 N/mm (riders >170 lb need 4.4-4.6), C8, R10, 3 mm up. Shock 48 N/mm, race sag 102 mm (he ran 105 for his size), HSC 1.25, LSC 11, R11. Jetting: 168 main, 62 pilot, Y4 needle clip 2, fuel screw 1-1.25 out; stock slightly rich; 165 main on pump gas; best on VP T2 or C12; prefers GYTR kit (leans bottom). Renthal 13/50 (stock 13/49, tested on 2024 at ~10 h): less clutch abuse, better pull in deep soil/hills, more 3rd in corners.

feedback.author: Rocket164, philepe747, Richard Tease II, digger, Alex814
feedback.conditions: Mostly sea level; 65-100 F; various fuels/premix
feedback.observed: Rocket164 (85-100 F, 32:1, C12/pump blend): 165 main, 62 pilot, Y3 clip 3; no change needed with PC pipe or APEX head. philepe747 (65-85 F): 162/65, NYEF clip 2, kept lowering pilot because plug loaded up. Richard Tease II (95-98 pump, 40:1): 162 main, 60 pilot, N3CG clip 3, go 1 leaner in summer. digger: 5.5 slide on 2023 YZ125X made it 'much easier to jet'. GYTR carb kit B4X-CARBS-KT-00 (Y3) said to be superseded by a Y4 kit.

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.observed: Standard: fork 4.4 N/mm, 5 mm, C9, R14; shock 50 N/mm, sag 104, LSC 9, HSC 1-1/8, R8. Keefer recommended (stock springs): fork 3 mm, C5, R12; shock LSC 6, HSC 1 turn, R7. 155-175 lb riders: 4.6 fork / 52 shock springs. Jetting needed no changes (Keihin PWK38S, same as 2021). Engine unchanged so past engine mods carry over.

feedback.author: Steve Havlicek (posted by Kris Keefer)
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen vet track; rider 6'1", 210-215 lb
feedback.observed: Sag 105 mm, forks to 'the first line'; jetted well out of the box; bars rolled forward; Dunlop MX33 no complaints. Suggests lowering pegs for tall riders (not tested).

feedback.author: Josh Fout
feedback.conditions: Milton IN singletrack + grass track; Ironman GNCC 12-mi loop, 2 h
feedback.observed: KYB lowered 10 mm (seat -15 mm) held up in fast grass, not harsh in singletrack. Long linear powerband; front mount 5->8 mm aided front-end response; 2.1 gal tank. Struggled to launch in gear - started in neutral then 2nd. GYTR handguards fitted (not stock).

feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.observed: Fork 4.8 N/mm (YZ450F 5.0), shock 56 (vs 58); 300 mm fork travel. Two clicks more fork compression fixed high-speed chop headshake. Wide-ratio 5-speed: 1st like +14 rear teeth, 2nd +6, 3rd +1, 4th -0.5, 5th -5 vs YZ450F. Map 1 (light off) aggressive, Map 2 tamer; free Power Tuner. Recommended: Twin Air PowerFlow (stock dome filter 'not foolproof'), GYTR hydraulic clutch fits, Nitromousse bibs for rocky West GP, handguards. 3 gal IMS tank fits.

feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: West coast fast desert/GP, east coast tight muddy woods, 24 Hours of Glen Helen
feedback.observed: Fork height stock 8 mm -> 5 mm too harsh with stock valving; settled 3 mm. Sag 100-102 (100 with valved suspension). Fork comp 2-6 clicks softer for most; shock HSC 1-5/8 out. Gearing stock 13/50 -> 14/52 (lighter/faster) or 14/53 (heavier): smoother delivery, more usable 2nd/3rd, better over acceleration chop. Map: stock zeros for fast west riders; 'JL GH' for vets; power scale 2 (map 1) / 3 (map 2) for technical. Removing front mount extra plate + YZ450F bolts (#187155035925) improved compliance, slightly less lean traction. Steel-braided front line recommended. Clutch plates/cables replaced ~40-44 h; oil every 5-7 h.

feedback.author: Mitch Kendra
feedback.observed: 125X preferred over 250X for comfort, easy pick-up, cheaper parts. 250X power delivery 'unpredictable' with drop-off at top of throttle but stronger on jumps/hills. 450FX stiffer/more composed fork than his 250F. 125X/250X carryover for 2024.

feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: West Coast GP/desert/MX + rocky singletrack; fork 3 mm, sag 100 mm; stock and revalved suspension
feedback.observed: Both gave the 23.5 mm stability gain. Ride: more comfort, less connected. Luxon: better front traction, precise but firm, slightly more fatigue (~5% comfort trade). Soft Luxon cones felt harsh to pros, medium better.

parts.observed: Quicker climb through power, more torque feel, 2nd usable in corners; $1,300

parts.observed: More bottom pull and rpm response; $945.99 kit w/o ECU
More mid, little more top; >1 lb lighter
Does not break down as quickly; $99.99

parts.observed: All testers felt it calmed steering
Slightly faster rev, more mid pull; no backfire screen

common_first_mods: Gearing: YZ250F 2024-2026 stock 13/50 -> 13/49 to stretch short 2nd gear (Keefer gearing guides 2024-2026; MXA 2025 YZ250F race test agrees).

Gearing on YZ450F disagrees by source: MXA went taller 49->48 on 2024/2025 to tame the hit; Keefer went shorter 13/50 for deep dirt or 14/52 for smoother roll-on. On 2026 (stock 13/51) Keefer goes 13/50; MXA says fast riders keep 51, vets like 50, 49 'not feasible'.

Power Tuner map: mellower map on 2023-2025 YZ450F (MXA ran the mellowest of several; Yamaha R&D map adds fuel 2000-5000 rpm); on YZ250F testers reduce engine braking/add response (MXA) or use Keefer 'Passive Aggressive'/'Free Feeling' maps.

Fork height: slide forks down / run flush-3 mm on 2023+ YZ450F and 2024+ YZ250F for stability (MXA, Keefer, Vital 2027 YZ250F) - but Swapmoto testers raised forks 5 mm on 2025 YZ450F; disagreement noted.
Triple clamps with more offset (23-24 mm) on 2023-2025 YZ450F: Luxon 23 mm (MXA), Ride Engineering 23.5 mm (Keefer), Xtrig ROCS 24 mm alternative.
Twin Air PowerFlow airbox kit (MXA YZ450F 2024/2025, YZ250F 2025, YZ450FX 2024; Keefer YZ250F) - note no backfire screen.
Aftermarket exhaust: FMF 4.1 or Pro Circuit preferred by MXA on YZ450F; FMF 4.1 adds mid on YZ250F (Keefer).
Seat foam/cover (Guts Racing) - stock seat shape criticized by MXA, Keefer, Dirt Bike Test across 2024-2026 YZ-F models.
Radiator cap upgrade to 1.8 kg/cm2 on YZ450F (MXA 2025 and 2026).
GYTR hydraulic clutch on cable-clutch YZ450F/YZ450FX (MXA); 2026 YZ450F and 2027 YZ250F/YZ450FX come with hydraulic clutch stock.
YZ125 2022+: richer-than-ideal stock jetting; GYTR/Pro Circuit Y4 needle kit, 13/50 gearing (Keefer); Vital forum owners lean pilot to 60-62.
YZ450FX 2024+: handguards (MXA, MXA GNCC), Nitromousse for rocks, 14/52-14/53 gearing and front-mount plate removal (Dirt Bike Test).
gaps: Platform boundaries confirmed from sources: YZ450F 2023 (new chassis/engine), 2025 (linkage, solid 8 mm front mounts, 56 N/mm shock), 2026 (new downtube, 4/6 mm mounts, new shock with tool-less LSC, hydraulic clutch, resonator exhaust, 13/51, password ECU); YZ250F 2024 (new frame/subframe/airbox), 2025 (linkage, 54 N/mm shock), 2027 (all-new engine, YZ450F-derived frame, new shock, hydraulic clutch); YZ450FX 2024 (2023 YZ450F platform), 2027 (new engine/frame, hydraulic clutch, 51T); YZ250FX 2025 (new gen); YZ125 2022 (new engine; YZ125X followed 2023 per Pro Circuit/FMF fitment).
